examples.en: The rice soup has big chunks of congealed blood in it.

examples.ko: 저는 선지를 처음 먹어 봤는데 맛이 괜찮았어요.
examples.en: It was my first time eating congealed blood, and it tasted fine.

examples.ko: 선지 냄새가 싫어서 빼 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I don't like the smell of congealed blood, so I asked them to leave it out.

examples.ko: 고기는 다 좋아하는데 선지는 잘 못 먹어요.
examples.en: I like all kinds of meat, but I can't really eat congealed blood.

examples.ko: 엄마가 끓여 준 선지국은 생각보다 고소했어요.
examples.en: The blood soup my mom made was more savory than I expected.

examples.ko: 선지를 안 먹는 친구도 이 집 국밥은 좋아해요.
examples.en: Even my friend who doesn't eat congealed blood likes this place's rice soup.

explain: 주로 소를 잡을 때 받은 피를 굳힌 것으로, 선지국이나 선지해장국 같은 국물 요리에 넣어요. 그냥 '피'라고 하면 음식 느낌이 안 나서 먹는 이야기에서는 '선지'라고 해요. 좋아하는 사람과 싫어하는 사람이 뚜렷이 갈리는 재료예요.
explain_en: It is mostly cattle blood that has been coagulated, and it goes into soups like 선지국. If you just say '피' (blood), it doesn't sound like food, so people say '선지' when talking about eating it. People tend to either love it or hate it.

examples.en: That director is a rising newcomer in the film world.

examples.ko: 신예 작가의 첫 소설이 베스트셀러가 됐어요.
examples.en: The young writer's first novel became a bestseller.

examples.ko: 이번 대회에는 신예 선수들이 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Many up-and-coming players took part in this competition.
This year's rookie award went to a rising star of the theater world.

examples.ko: 신예 가수 중에서 누구를 가장 좋아해요?
examples.en: Among the up-and-coming singers, who do you like the most?

examples.ko: 그 팀은 신예와 베테랑이 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: On that team, the rising stars and the veterans work well together.

explain: '신인'은 막 시작한 사람이면 누구나 가리키지만, '신예'는 새로 나타났는데 실력이 눈에 띈다는 느낌이 있어요. 작가, 감독, 선수 앞에 붙이거나 '신예로 떠오르다'처럼 뉴스와 기사에서 자주 보여요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '베테랑', '노장'이에요.
explain_en: '신인' simply means someone who has just started, but '신예' also suggests that the person stands out for their talent. It is often attached before writers, directors and athletes, or used like '신예로 떠오르다' in news articles. The opposite feeling is '베테랑' or '노장'.

examples.en: The plane landed safely at the airport.

examples.ko: 새 학교에 안착하기까지 한 달쯤 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took about a month to settle into the new school.

examples.ko: 이사 온 가족이 새 동네에 잘 안착했어요.
examples.en: The family that moved in has settled into the new neighborhood well.

examples.ko: 신입 사원이 회사에 안착할 수 있게 도와줘요.
examples.en: We help new employees settle into the company.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 시장에 안착하는 데 성공했어요.
examples.en: This app succeeded in establishing itself in the market.

examples.ko: 새 제도가 안착하려면 시간이 더 필요해요.
examples.en: The new system needs more time to take hold.

explain: 어딘가에 안전하게 내려앉는다는 느낌이 있어서 비행기나 우주선에도 쓰고, 새 환경이나 제도, 서비스가 자리를 잡을 때 비유로도 많이 써요. '정착하다'는 한곳에 오래 자리 잡고 사는 느낌이 강하고, '안착하다'는 무사히 도착해서 안정된 순간에 초점이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '자리를 잡다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of landing safely somewhere, so it is used for planes and spacecraft, and figuratively when a new environment, system or service takes hold. '정착하다' stresses settling down for a long time, while '안착하다' focuses on the moment of arriving safely and becoming stable. In everyday talk people also say '자리를 잡다'.

en: arrange; broker; help find (a job, housing)

examples.en: The district office helps find jobs for senior citizens.

examples.ko: 이 센터는 유학생에게 집을 알선하기도 해요.
examples.en: This center also arranges housing for international students.

examples.ko: 선배가 아르바이트 자리를 알선해 줘서 고마웠어요.
examples.en: I was thankful that my senior helped me find a part-time job.
The travel agency said it would arrange a hotel for us.
The company arranged a dormitory for the new employees.

examples.ko: 돈을 받고 알선하는 사람은 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You should be careful with people who arrange things for money.

explain: 중간에서 사람과 일자리, 집 같은 것을 이어 주는 일에 써요. 기관이나 업체가 주어일 때 자연스럽고, 친구 사이에서는 보통 '소개해 주다'라고 해요. '일자리 알선', '알선 업체'처럼 명사로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when someone in the middle connects people with things like jobs or housing. It sounds natural with an organization or business as the subject, while between friends people usually say '소개해 주다'. It also appears as a noun, as in '일자리 알선' and '알선 업체'.

examples.en: The puppy wagging its tail looks so endearing.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 말투가 애교스러워서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That child is popular because of the charming way he talks.
It's hard to refuse when someone asks in a cute, charming voice.
My younger sibling charmingly asked for some pocket money.
The cat rubbed against my leg in an endearing way.

examples.ko: 애교스럽지 않은 성격이라 이런 건 어색해요.
examples.en: I'm not the charming type, so this feels awkward.

explain: '귀엽다'는 겉모습에도 쓰지만, '애교스럽다'는 상냥하고 사랑스러운 말투나 행동에 더 많이 써요. 사람과 동물 모두에게 쓰고, '애교를 부리다'와 함께 알아 두면 좋아요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '애교스러워요', '애교스러운'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: '귀엽다' can describe looks too, but '애교스럽다' is used more for sweet, lovable speech and behavior. It applies to both people and animals, and it pairs well with '애교를 부리다'. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '애교스러워요' and '애교스러운'.

examples.en: There is a really wide variety of fish species in this river.

examples.ko: 어종마다 잡을 수 있는 시기가 달라요.
examples.en: The season when you can catch them differs for each fish species.

examples.ko: 낚시를 하기 전에 어떤 어종이 많은지 알아봤어요.
examples.en: Before fishing, I checked which fish species are common.
I saw news that a new fish species was discovered.

examples.ko: 외국에서 들어온 어종 때문에 생태계가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: The ecosystem changed because of a fish species brought in from abroad.
At the raw fish restaurant, I asked which fish came in today.

explain: '물고기 종류'를 한 단어로 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '물고기 종류'라고 많이 하고, '어종'은 낚시, 횟집, 뉴스, 환경 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 셀 때는 '몇 종'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a single word for 'kinds of fish'. In daily talk people often just say '물고기 종류', while '어종' shows up in fishing, sashimi restaurants, news and environmental topics. To count them, you say '몇 종'.

examples.ko: 아버지가 세계 문학 전집을 사 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father bought me a complete collection of world literature.

examples.ko: 그 작가의 전집이 드디어 다 나왔어요.
examples.en: The complete works of that author have finally all come out.
I borrowed a full set of fairy tales from the library.

examples.ko: 전집으로 사면 한 권씩 사는 것보다 싸요.
examples.en: Buying the whole set is cheaper than buying one book at a time.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 읽던 전집이 아직 책장에 있어요.
examples.en: The book set I read as a kid is still on the shelf.

examples.ko: 이 전집은 열 권으로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This collection consists of ten volumes.

explain: 한 작가의 작품이나 한 주제의 책을 세트로 묶은 것이에요. 한 권씩 따로 파는 '낱권'과 반대되고, 어린이 책이나 세계 문학처럼 '동화 전집', '○○ 전집'으로 많이 불러요.
explain_en: It is a set of books bundled together, either by one author or one theme. It is the opposite of buying single volumes ('낱권'), and is commonly used in names like '동화 전집' or '○○ 전집', especially for children's books and world literature.

examples.ko: 친구의 조력 덕분에 일이 빨리 끝났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my friend's help, the work finished quickly.

examples.ko: 이번 일은 여러분의 조력이 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: This job really needs everyone's support.
I made the plan with an expert's assistance.
If I hadn't had a helper, I would have given up.
He worked as my father's assistant for a long time.
I'm truly grateful for the villagers' help.

explain: '도움'보다 딱딱하고 글이나 공식적인 자리에서 더 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '도움'이라고 하고, '조력자'는 이야기나 뉴스에서 곁에서 돕는 사람을 가리킬 때 자주 써요. '조력을 받다', '조력을 얻다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than '도움' and fits writing or formal situations better. In everyday talk people say '도움', and '조력자' is often used in stories and news for someone who helps from the side. It is used as '조력을 받다' or '조력을 얻다'.

en: mid-level; established (core member of a field); mid-sized

examples.ko: 그 회사는 직원 수가 많은 중견 기업이에요.
examples.en: That company is a mid-sized firm with many employees.
As a seasoned actor, he takes good care of his juniors.

examples.ko: 저는 대기업보다 중견 기업에서 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work at a mid-sized company rather than a big corporation.

examples.ko: 중견 작가의 새 소설이 이번 주에 나와요.
examples.en: A new novel by an established writer comes out this week.
The mid-career staff are the busiest on the team.

examples.ko: 그는 이제 업계의 중견으로 인정받고 있어요.
examples.en: He is now recognized as an established figure in the industry.

explain: 신입도 아니고 원로도 아닌, 한 분야에서 중심을 잡고 있는 믿을 만한 사람을 가리켜요. '중견 기업'은 대기업과 중소기업의 중간 규모 회사를 말하고, '중견 배우', '중견 작가'처럼 자주 써요. 새로 나온 사람을 말하는 '신예'와 대비해서 외워 두세요.
explain_en: It points to a reliable person who is neither a newcomer nor a senior elder, but is carrying a field. '중견 기업' means a company between large and small ones, and it is often used as in '중견 배우' and '중견 작가'. Remember it in contrast with '신예', which means a newcomer.

examples.en: The enemy troops finally threw down their weapons and surrendered.
He held out to the end and then decided to surrender.
Many soldiers opened the castle gate and surrendered.

examples.ko: 투항하지 않으면 큰 피해가 날 거라고 했어요.
examples.en: They said that there would be heavy losses if they didn't surrender.
I saw a scene in a historical drama where a general surrenders.
The fleeing soldiers began to surrender one by one.

explain: 전쟁이나 싸움에서 상대편에게 가서 항복한다는 느낌이에요. '항복하다'는 시합이나 말싸움에도 쓰지만 '투항하다'는 군사나 역사 이야기에서 주로 나와요. 일상에서 장난으로 '항복!'이라고 말하는 것과는 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of going over to the other side and giving up in a war or battle. '항복하다' can also be used for games and arguments, but '투항하다' appears mainly in military and history contexts. It is different from jokingly saying '항복!' in daily life.

examples.en: A good leader embraces different opinions too.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 누구든 포용하는 넓은 마음을 가졌어요.
examples.en: That person has a big heart that accepts anyone.

examples.ko: 서로 다른 문화를 포용하는 사회가 되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope we become a society that embraces different cultures.

examples.ko: 엄마는 제 실수를 늘 포용해 주세요.
examples.en: My mom always forgives my mistakes with understanding.
It's not easy to accept even a friend's faults.

examples.ko: 다양한 사람을 포용할 줄 아는 사람이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be a person who knows how to embrace all kinds of people.

explain: '받아들이다'와 비슷하지만 상대의 다름이나 잘못까지 넓은 마음으로 감싸 준다는 느낌이 있어요. '이해하다'보다 따뜻하고 큰 마음을 나타내요. '포용력이 있다', '포용적인 사회'처럼 명사 형태도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '받아들이다' but adds the feeling of wrapping up even another person's differences or faults with a big heart. It sounds warmer and larger-hearted than '이해하다'. Forms like '포용력이 있다' and '포용적인 사회' are also common.

examples.en: The stock price plunged in a single day.
Cabbage prices collapsed because of a bumper harvest.

examples.ko: 집값이 폭락할까 봐 걱정하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people worry that housing prices will plummet.
Crypto prices crashed, and he was very upset.
When prices collapsed, the farmers sighed.
Don't touch stocks that suddenly nosedive.

explain: 값이나 시세가 갑자기 크게 떨어질 때 써요. 그냥 '떨어지다'보다 훨씬 급하고 큰 변화이고, 반대말은 '폭등하다'예요. 가격, 주가, 시세에 주로 쓰고 사람의 기분이나 점수에는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a price or market value suddenly falls by a large amount. It is much sharper and bigger than plain '떨어지다', and its opposite is '폭등하다'. It is used mainly for prices, stock values and market rates, and not usually for a person's mood or scores.

examples.en: The retired professor published a memoir.
My grandfather has recently started writing his memoirs.

examples.ko: 이 회고록에는 어린 시절 이야기가 많아요.
examples.en: This memoir has many stories from childhood.
Politicians' memoirs always become a topic of conversation.
After reading the memoir, I became curious about that era.
I want to leave behind a memoir someday too.

explain: 자기가 겪은 일을 돌아보며 직접 쓴 책이에요. '자서전'이 보통 인생 전체를 다루는 데 비해, 회고록은 기억에 남는 시기나 경험을 중심으로 쓰는 경우가 많아요. '회고록을 쓰다', '회고록을 내다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a book a person writes themselves while looking back on what they have experienced. While an '자서전' (autobiography) usually covers a whole life, a memoir often centers on a memorable period or experience. It is used as '회고록을 쓰다' or '회고록을 내다'.

examples.ko: 충전 중에 휴대폰이 과열돼서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: My phone overheated while charging, and I was startled.

examples.ko: 경쟁이 너무 과열되어서 분위기가 안 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: The competition became so heated that the atmosphere turned bad.
When a laptop overheats, the fan gets louder.
I'm worried that the real estate market will overheat.

examples.ko: 과열된 입시 경쟁을 줄이자는 이야기가 나왔어요.
examples.en: People started talking about reducing the overheated entrance exam competition.
The engine overheated, so I stopped the car for a moment.

explain: 기계가 너무 뜨거워질 때도 쓰고, 경쟁이나 시장, 분위기가 지나치게 뜨거워질 때 비유로도 많이 써요. '과열 경쟁', '과열 양상'처럼 명사로 뒤 말을 꾸미기도 해요. 열을 내리는 말로는 '식히다', '식다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when a machine gets too hot, and also figuratively when competition, a market or the mood becomes too intense. The noun form often modifies another word, as in '과열 경쟁'. For cooling down, you can use '식히다' or '식다'.

examples.en: He is in a detention center waiting for his trial.
My friend said he went to visit someone at the detention center.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 구치소 앞 모습을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The news showed the scene in front of the detention center.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 말하는 구치소와 교도소는 어떻게 달라요?
examples.en: How are the detention centers and prisons mentioned in the news different?

examples.ko: 구치소에서 지내는 사람들도 규칙을 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: People staying in a detention center also have to follow the rules.

examples.ko: 그 영화에는 구치소가 나오는 장면이 있어요.
examples.en: That movie has a scene set in a detention center.

explain: 아직 재판을 받는 중이거나 기다리는 사람이 머무는 곳이에요. 형이 정해진 사람이 가는 '교도소'와 달라서 뉴스에서는 두 말을 구분해 써요. 보통 '구치소에 수감되다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is where people who are on trial or waiting for trial are held. It differs from '교도소', where people with a final sentence go, and the news keeps the two words apart. It usually appears as in '구치소에 수감되다'.

examples.en: Christianity is a religion with many followers around the world.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 그리스도교 문화의 영향을 받았어요.
examples.en: This building was influenced by Christian culture.
The big holidays of Christianity are Christmas and Easter.
We learned about the history of Christianity in class.

examples.ko: 유럽 미술에는 그리스도교 이야기가 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Christian stories often appear in European art.

examples.ko: 그리스도교 신자인 친구와 성당에 가 봤어요.
examples.en: I went to a cathedral with a friend who is a Christian.

explain: 가톨릭, 개신교 등을 모두 포함해서 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '기독교'라고 더 자주 하고, 한국에서는 '기독교'가 개신교만 가리키는 경우도 많아요. '그리스도교'는 수업이나 설명, 글에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used to cover Catholicism, Protestantism and others all together. In daily conversation '기독교' is more common, and in Korea '기독교' often refers to Protestantism only. '그리스도교' shows up more in classes, explanations and writing.

examples.en: He decided the matter on his own, without consulting anyone.
The team members are struggling because of the team leader's high-handedness.

examples.ko: 독단적인 행동은 팀 분위기를 해칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: Arbitrary behavior can hurt the team atmosphere.

examples.ko: 독단에 빠지지 않으려면 남의 말도 들어야 해요.
examples.en: To avoid being dogmatic, you have to listen to others too.

examples.ko: 이런 큰일을 제 독단으로 정할 수는 없어요.
examples.en: I can't decide such a big matter on my own.

examples.ko: 독단으로 계약을 바꿨다가 큰 문제가 생겼어요.
examples.en: He changed the contract without consulting anyone, and a big problem arose.

explain: 다른 사람과 상의하지 않고 혼자 결정하는 것을 나쁘게 말할 때 써요. '독단으로', '독단적이다', '독단에 빠지다'가 자주 쓰이는 형태예요. 비슷한 말로 '독선'이 있는데, 자기 생각만 옳다고 믿는 태도를 더 강조해요.
explain_en: It is used, with a negative tone, for deciding things alone without consulting others. Common forms are '독단으로', '독단적이다' and '독단에 빠지다'. A similar word is '독선', which puts more weight on the attitude of believing only your own view is right.

examples.en: The landlord pressed me to pay the rent.
The company keeps urging us to hand in the report quickly.
If you keep pushing, I end up not wanting to work.

examples.ko: 도서관에서 책을 반납하라고 독촉하는 문자가 왔어요.
examples.en: I got a text from the library urging me to return the book.
Please don't nag your child to do the homework.
It's hard to press my friend about the money I lent.

explain: 돈, 서류, 기한처럼 해야 할 일을 빨리 하라고 계속 재촉할 때 써요. '재촉하다'가 더 넓게 쓰이고, '독촉하다'는 갚아야 할 돈이나 내야 할 것에 특히 자주 나와요. '독촉장', '독촉 전화'처럼 명사로도 써요.
explain_en: It is used when you keep pressing someone to do something they owe, such as money, documents or deadlines. '재촉하다' has a broader range, while '독촉하다' appears especially often with money to be repaid or things to be handed in. It also works as a noun, as in '독촉장' and '독촉 전화'.

examples.en: A batter came up in the bottom of the ninth with the bases loaded.
A grand slam was hit, and the stadium got fired up.
The pitcher got through the bases-loaded jam well.
When the bases were loaded, the whole crowd stood up.

examples.ko: 저는 만루에서 삼진을 당하는 장면이 제일 아쉬워요.
examples.en: The most disappointing thing for me is a strikeout with the bases loaded.
The team lost after missing a bases-loaded chance.

explain: 야구에서 1루, 2루, 3루에 모두 주자가 있는 상황을 말해요. '만루 홈런', '만루 위기', '만루 찬스'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 자주 써요. 소리는 [말루]로 나요.
explain_en: In baseball, it means runners are on first, second and third base all at once. It is often placed before other words, as in '만루 홈런', '만루 위기' and '만루 찬스'. It is pronounced [말루].

examples.en: New cultural products and systems came in after the ports opened.
The students who studied abroad brought back Western knowledge and ways.
I looked at relics from an earlier era at the museum.

examples.ko: 여행은 다른 나라의 문물을 직접 보는 좋은 기회예요.
examples.en: Travel is a good chance to see another country's culture firsthand.

examples.ko: 외국 문물이 빠르게 퍼지면서 생활이 달라졌어요.
examples.en: As foreign culture spread quickly, daily life changed.

examples.ko: 그 도시는 다양한 문물이 모이는 곳이에요.
examples.en: That city is a place where varied cultural goods and ideas gather.

explain: 한 사회의 제도, 기술, 물건 같은 문화의 결과물을 두루 가리켜요. 주로 '새로운 문물', '서양 문물', '외국 문물'처럼 역사나 교류를 설명할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '문화'나 '물건'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: It broadly refers to the products of a society's culture, such as institutions, technology and objects. It is mostly used when explaining history or exchange, as in '새로운 문물', '서양 문물' and '외국 문물'. In daily talk people usually say '문화' or '물건' instead.
